general.label: Pretrial detention vs. release
general.q: When someone is charged with a serious crime (but not yet convicted), should judges have broader power to keep them in jail if the evidence looks strong and the person appears to pose a safety risk to others?
general.a: Keep the constitutional right to bail strong; expand detention authority only with extreme caution because people are presumed innocent.
general.b: Give judges clearer tools to detain high-risk defendants before trial when evidence is strong and no conditions can reasonably protect the community.

general.label: Local residency for judges
general.q: Should city and town court judges be required to live inside the municipality they serve, or should the residency rule be relaxed so more qualified lawyers can serve (especially in smaller communities)?
general.a: Judges should live in the community they serve so they understand local people and conditions.
general.b: Relax residency rules so rural and small communities can recruit from a wider pool of qualified attorneys.

general.label: Election administration emphasis
general.q: In running elections and business filings, which should the Secretary of State emphasize more?
general.a: Broad access, participation, and independent oversight of the office itself.
general.b: Strict integrity measures, fraud prevention in filings and voting, and conservative stewardship of the office.

general.label: Taxes and government size
general.q: In general, when state or local government faces budget pressure, which direction do you prefer?
general.a: Maintain or expand services even if it means higher taxes or fees.
general.b: Keep taxes and spending lower, even if some services are reduced or delayed.

general.label: Approach to crime and prosecution
general.q: Overall, should the justice system lean more toward longer detention and stricter enforcement, or toward alternatives that reduce incarceration where possible?
general.a: Favor alternatives, treatment, and lower incarceration when public safety allows.
general.b: Favor stronger detention tools, prosecution, and accountability for those who pose risks.

general.label: Party control of government
general.q: All else equal, do you generally prefer Republican or Democratic leadership in state and county offices?
general.a: Prefer Democratic or independent leadership on balance.

general.label: Immigration and border policy
general.q: How should the federal government handle border security and immigration enforcement?
general.a: Emphasize pathways, humane processing, and targeted enforcement over broad crackdowns.
general.b: Emphasize stronger border control, enforcement, and limits on illegal entry.

general.label: Government role in local economy
general.q: When local industries face pressure (tariffs, regulation, competition), what role should government play?
general.a: More active support, targeted help, or protection for local jobs and industries.
general.b: Lower taxes, less regulation, and let markets and private investment drive outcomes.

general.label: Support for local law enforcement
general.q: How should county government approach funding and policy for the sheriff and prosecutor?
general.a: Balance enforcement with community programs and oversight of police power.
general.b: Prioritize strong funding, tools, and backing for law enforcement and prosecution.

general.label: Amending the state constitution
general.q: In general, how cautious should voters be about amending the Indiana Constitution?
general.a: Very cautious; the document should change only for clear, narrow needs.
general.b: Willing to update the constitution when the legislature and voters see a practical problem.

general.label: Office accountability
general.q: When an elected office has faced ethics or spending questions, what is the better first step?
general.a: Independent outside audit and structural reform of the office.
general.b: Internal investigation by existing state mechanisms plus tighter day-to-day management.

tags.why: Yes expands constitutional authority to deny bail beyond murder/treason when proof is evident/presumption strong and state proves by clear-and-convincing evidence that no conditions protect safety.
Moves system toward greater pretrial detention power based on risk prediction.
Amends long-standing (1851) constitutional right to bail.

quality.detail: Amendment is not limited to violent offenses; critics note it could apply to a wide range of charges (including some misdemeanors) if a judge finds the two conditions met. Companion statute (SEA 2) sets procedure but does not take effect until Jan 1 2027, creating a short window of constitutional authority without the new hearing rules.
If approved, the constitutional change takes effect at poll close on Election Day per Indiana precedent, while implementing statute is delayed.

tags.why: Yes expands where city/town court judges may reside (county of the court or closest bordering Indiana county) instead of requiring residence inside the municipality.
Amends Article 6, Section 6 residency rule for a narrow class of judges.

items.note: Supporters cite attorney shortages in rural areas that make it hard to find local candidates; opponents argue judges should live in the communities they serve. The 'closest bordering county' is calculated by shortest distance from city/town limits to the county line. Source: https://ballotpedia.org/Indiana_Public_Question_2,_Residency_Requirements_for_City_and_Town_Court_Judges_Amendment_(2026)
